explanation: Raw candidate n of GRU unit 41. Timing alone gives R^2 0.73 (strongly negative at GO, rising with episode time at D1/D2). Beyond timing it is driven mainly at D1 by the previous trial: positive when the last trial reached S2 (a1 S2 u +0.98, a1 S2 r +0.71, a2 S2 u +0.50) and negative when it reached S1 (a2 S1 r -0.66, a2 S1 u -0.58, a1 S1 r -0.24). So it roughly encodes last state S2 vs S1, made stronger by a rare transition and, for S2, by no reward. At D2 it is positive after an unrewarded previous trial (+0.20), and carries the sign of the current rare transition (a1->S2 +0.33, a2->S1 -0.33), slightly lower after a rewarded a2 trial. GO residuals are tiny. The trial before last, good state and since-reversal add little. Remaining misses: the first trial of a window (previous trial unknown) and saturation late in the episode. 4 observed-only terms (D2 terms use this trial choice/state, observed at D2): dev 0.74 beyond timing; all ceiling 0.83, all observed 0.77.

issues: The scores reproduce: the 4 terms give test R^2 beyond timing 0.739, against an 'all observed' ceiling of 0.77. No future variables are used. Misses show no large systematic class: mean error by phase is +0.005 at D1, +0.014 at GO and -0.019 at D2, and the worst (phase x last trial) cells are only about +/-0.1 (D2 after a1 S2 u +0.115, D2 after a2 S1 u -0.104). The worst single windows are first-trial D1 steps where the previous trial is unknown, as the explanation says.

The headline 'high after S2, low after S1' misreads the D1 effect. A factorial fit puts almost no weight on the state reached: (D1)*(prev_state==S2) gets +0.03 to +0.07. The weight sits on the rare transition signed by state: rare->S2 minus rare->S1 gets +0.73 (test R^2 0.70 for the factorial set vs 0.739). The D1 residuals agree: after common trials the activation is near zero, a2 S2 r -0.03 and a1 S1 u +0.05. Only rare trials go strongly in each direction: a1 S2 +0.98/+0.71, a2 S1 -0.66/-0.58.

Being unrewarded raises the activation after any common trial, not just after S2 as the explanation implies (a1 S1 u +0.05 vs a1 S1 r -0.24; a2 S2 u +0.50 vs a2 S2 r -0.03). In the factorial fit the unrewarded term gets +0.19, and the unrewarded a2->S2 interaction adds another +0.32.
The label says 'esp. rare a1->S2' but leaves out that rare a2->S1 gives the most negative values. The D1 code is symmetric in the rare transition, not an S2-specific effect.

Small points: adding the trial before last or (D2)*(prev_action==action) adds at most 0.005 (0.744). The internal policy logit 'choice' at D1/D2 adds about 0.05 (0.789), but it is a model-output cue, not an observed one. The D2 claims hold (prev unrewarded +0.20; current rare transition a1->S2 +0.33, a2->S1 -0.33).
